items.title: Governments make over 230 new pledges to prevent violence against children
items.summary: Governments are stepping up action to protect children from violence, with over 230 new pledges to be announced at the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children in Manila, Philippines taking place on 18-19 November, the World Health Organization (WHO) said today. items.title: Evidence mounts that exposure to hormone-disrupting chemicals starts before birth: UNEP–WHO report
items.summary: The State of the Science on Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals 2026 report, is the first major global update since the 2012 UNEP-WHO assessment; it finds that more than a decade of research has strengthened and broadened the evidence linking these chemicals with harm to people and wildlife.

items.title: Countries expand cervical cancer screening and treatment, bringing elimination closer
items.summary: Three in five women aged 30–49 have never been screened for cervical cancer, according to new WHO estimates. Access to human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is particularly unequal. Only 2% of women in low- and middle-income countries were screened using HPV testing in the preceding five years, compared with 32% in high-income countries.

items.title: More countries have antimicrobial resistance plans but patients still lack testing and treatment
items.summary: As more countries are taking steps to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), major gaps that remain in testing and treatment mean that many patients are still at risk, according to new data from the World Health Organization (WHO).When medicines lose their effectiveness against resistant bacteria and other microbes, common infections become harder to treat and routine medical procedures, including surgery, childbirth and cancer care, become riskier. items.title: Eritrea eliminates trachoma: a major public health milestone
items.summary: The WHO has validated Eritrea's elimination of trachoma as a public health problem, making it the 11th country in WHO’s African Region and the 34th globally to reach this major milestone.

items.title: WHO issues first guidelines on type 1 diabetes for adults
items.summary: More than 100 years after the discovery of insulin, many people living with type 1 diabetes still cannot access the insulin and care they need to survive. Marking World Diabetes Day 2026, WHO has issued its first guidelines on the diagnosis and management of type 1 diabetes in adults, with recommendations designed to apply across all settings, including low-resource, emergency and humanitarian settings.

items.title: Put health in the treaty: youth delegates at the Global Model WHO 2026 adopt declaration on plastics and health
items.summary: This week at WHO headquarters in Geneva, more than 400 young leaders from over 50 countries and all six WHO regions called on governments to protect human health from the preventable harms of plastics.

items.title: Member States reiterate commitment to finalize Pandemic Agreement PABS Annex by May 2027
items.summary: Member States advanced negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) Annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement, reaffirming their commitment to finalizing the Annex for its consideration by the World Health Assembly in May 2027. The PABS Annex would establish a system that ensures the rapid, transparent sharing of pathogens with pandemic potential and their genetic sequence data, while ensuring rapid and equitable access to the resulting products, including vaccines, diagnostics and t

items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) – Qatar
items.summary: On 29 October 2026, the National International Health Regulations (IHR) Focal Point of the State of Qatar notified the World Health Organization (WHO) of two laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS). The cases were confirmed on 5 and 25 August 2026 and are the first MERS cases reported from Qatar since 2022. items.title: Statement of the Forty-sixth Meeting of the Polio IHR Emergency Committee
items.summary: The 46th meeting of the Emergency Committee under the International Health Regulations (IHR or Regulations) on the international spread of poliovirus was convened by the WHO Director-General on 30 September 2026 via video conference with affected countries, supported by the WHO Secretariat.

items.title: Conflict and disease outbreaks deepen DR Congo’s hunger crisis as record numbers are projected to face acute food insecurity
items.summary: FAO, WFP, UNICEF and WHO call for urgent action as acute hunger is projected to hit more than 30 million, including 4.2 million people facing Emergency levels of hunger in early 2027.

items.title: Amid challenges, countries increase domestic investment to protect progress against tuberculosis
items.summary: Global efforts to end tuberculosis (TB) continue to make progress, with fewer people falling ill and dying from the disease, according to the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released today.

items.title: WHO calls for migrant-inclusive primary health care to strengthen health systems for all
items.summary: Developed by the WHO Health and Migration Programme in collaboration with WHO’s Service Delivery and Primary Health Care Unit, the report examines how primary health care-oriented responses can improve access, continuity and quality of care for people on the move, while strengthening health systems for diverse populations.

items.title: Bangladesh and India ban toxic pesticide to boost suicide prevention and brain health
items.summary: Regulatory action on an acutely toxic pesticide will save thousands of lives and protect brain health worldwideGlobally it is estimated 1 in 5 suicides are attributable to the ingestion of acutely toxic pesticides. Many of these deaths are easily preventable and occur in rural communities across Africa, Asia, Eastern Mediterranean, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific Islands. items.title: WHO and African Medicines Agency advance regulatory cooperation at inaugural Agency Week in Kigali
items.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening Africa's regulatory systems during the inaugural African Medicines Agency (AMA) Week and the 11th African Medicines Regulators Conference (AMRC), held from 25 to 30 October 2026 in Kigali, Rwanda. items.title: WHO launches “Together for Science and Health” movement to strengthen trust worldwide
items.summary: WHO today launched Together for Science and Health, a new global movement uniting more than 240 organizations behind a shared commitment to strengthen trust in science and harness its power to improve health and development.

items.summary: Since the publication of the previous Disease Outbreak News on 23 October 2026, the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak has expanded geographically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. While some areas have seen a slight decline in cases, sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. items.title: Yellow fever - WHO African Region
items.summary: Yellow fever transmission continues in the WHO African Region, with recent outbreak activity concentrated in parts of West Africa. Between 1 January and 12 October 2026, 67 confirmed cases, including 18 deaths, were recorded in nine countries in the Region: Burkina Faso, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria and Togo. items.title: Shamonda virus in human - France
items.summary: On 20 October 2026, the National IHR Focal Point (NFP) of France notified WHO regarding the first documented human infection with Shamonda virus (SHAV). The case was an immunocompromised older man from eastern France with no travel history during the preceding year. He developed severe neurological illness on 23 September 2026 and was diagnosed with severe encephalitis (brain inflammation). The patient died on 8 October 2026. items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Between 1 January and 5 October 2026, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection, including one death. Cases were detected across six locations: Al Jouf (1), Arar (1), Hafr Al-Batin (1), Riyadh (2), Tabuk (1) and Taif (2). No epidemiological links were identified between any of the cases. According to these reports, the individual died on 2 October following hospitalization for severe pneumonia on 29 September, and pneumonic plague was suspected as the cause of death, following occupational exposure in laboratory settings. items.summary: On 5 October 2026, WHO was informed about a laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Kenya with travel history from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The patient travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Kenya through Uganda. The patient was hospitalized and treated in Kenya but subsequently died on 5 October. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 11 September 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with two additional health zones affected. These include Bulu health zone in a new province, Sud Ubangi, located on the north-west part of the country and Dungu health zone in Haut-Uélé province, bordering South Sudan. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 28 August 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to one additional health zone, Kayna, in North Kivu.
